title: JeffersonWM widget auth privacy and service task checkpoint
content:
This checkpoint closes the day around two related pieces of platform housekeeping: making the JeffersonWM widget privacy model real, and making the server task system match the new service boundaries.

The important direction change is that widget personalization is now treated as JeffersonWM-owned account data rather than a loose public widget feed. Earlier transition work left us with useful scaffolding, but the privacy question made the next step clear: guests should see safe defaults, regular users should see only their own data, and admin-only legacy/global dates should stop leaking through old widget routes.

What worked:

  • Auth status instead of cookie guessing: JeffersonWM now asks Auth for the actual session state instead of assuming that the presence of a cookie means a usable user. That gives the widget access to approved, blocked, deleted, and admin state.
  • Option-1 privacy model: guests receive the San Francisco default widget with no special-date data, signed-in users receive only their own widget preferences and personal dates, and admin can still see/manage the existing legacy/global widget dates.
  • Admin-only legacy routes: older direct event endpoints were tightened so legacy special-date data cannot be fetched casually by guests or regular users.
  • Runtime labels now match the architecture: the shared task system now has separate jeffwm server and jeffwm tunnel entries, while the old peri/jeffwm tunnel label was renamed to peri tunnel.

What changed:

  • Updated the JeffersonWM widget API to call https://auth.jeffersonwm.com/api/auth/status for real user resolution.
  • Changed account/widget preference and personal-date writes so they require an approved signed-in Auth user.
  • Kept guest widget state intentionally empty except for safe defaults.
  • Copied the updated JeffersonWM server file to the server share.
  • Added JeffersonWM server/tunnel entries to the shared launcher and VS Code task files.
  • Confirmed Copy and Aphelion server/tunnel entries are included in the grouped start, stop, and restart flows.
  • Added api-jeffersonwm.token and E:\jeffersonwm\ to stop/restart tracking.

What did not hold up:

  • The old cookie-name shortcut was too imprecise for privacy work. It could identify that something auth-like existed, but not who the user was or whether that user should have access.
  • The older Perihelion/JeffersonWM shared tunnel label was useful during migration, but it became misleading once JeffersonWM had its own API identity.

Verification passed with a JeffersonWM build, lint, JSON task parsing, and PowerShell launcher readback. The next live step is simply to restart the JeffersonWM server when ready, then publish/copy the static build if the frontend widget changes need to be reflected publicly.
